title: India's Shifting Wealth Pyramid: What FY31 Could Bring
description: India is experiencing a rapid transformation in its household income distribution. Millions of families are steadily moving into higher income brackets, boost.

faq.q: What is the "income pyramid" in India?
faq.a: The income pyramid visually represents the distribution of household incomes, with the largest number of households at the lowest income levels forming the base and progressively fewer households at higher income levels towards the top. India's pyramid is becoming less broad at the bottom and wider in the middle.

faq.q: How does rising income affect my taxes?
faq.a: As your income increases, you may move into higher income tax slabs, leading to a larger portion of your income being taxed at a higher rate. It becomes crucial to explore tax-efficient investment avenues and deductions to optimise your tax liability.

faq.q: Should I change my investments if my income increases?
faq.a: Yes, it's advisable to review and potentially adjust your investment strategy. With higher income, you might have a greater capacity for risk, allowing you to diversify into growth-oriented assets like equities or real estate, and focus on long-term wealth creation.

Lifestyle creep refers to the phenomenon where an individual's spending increases in proportion to their rising income. This can make it difficult to save or invest more, even with a higher salary, as increased earnings are absorbed by upgraded living standards and discretionary purchases.

faq.q: Is this trend of upward mobility sustainable?
faq.a: While economic growth can fluctuate, the underlying drivers like formalisation, urbanisation, and skill development suggest a sustainable long-term trend of upward income mobility for a significant portion of the Indian population. Government policies also aim to support this growth.

faq.q: How can NRIs benefit from this shift in India's wealth pyramid?
faq.a: NRIs can benefit by investing in India's growing economy through various channels like NRE/NRO accounts, PIS (Portfolio Investment Scheme) for equities, and real estate. The rising disposable incomes indicate a growing consumer market and potential for higher returns on well-chosen investments.

based_on.title: More households are moving up the income ladder: How India's wealth pyramid could change by FY31
